definitions.explanation: An abstract idea or general understanding of something.

examples.japanese: {基本的|きほんてき}な{概念|がいねん}を{理解|りかい}する。
「{自由|じゆう}」という{概念|がいねん}について{考|かんが}える。
この{概念|がいねん}は{日本語|にほんご}にはない。
examples.english: This concept doesn't exist in Japanese.

notes:
{概念|がいねん} is a compound: {概|がい} (outline/general) + {念|ねん} (idea).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {概念|がいねん}を{理解|りかい}する (to understand a concept)
- {概念|がいねん}を{持|も}つ (to have a concept/notion)
- {概念|がいねん}{的|てき}（な） (conceptual)
- {抽象|ちゅうしょう}{概念|がいねん} (abstract concept)
- {固定|こてい}{概念|がいねん} (fixed idea, preconception)

RELATED VOCABULARY:
- {考|かんが}え (thought, idea - more casual)
- {観念|かんねん} (notion, sense)
- {理念|りねん} (ideology, principle)

ACademic/technical contexts often use {概念|がいねん} when discussing abstract or theoretical ideas.
